doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Henry Grant gives him a flute; Wayman Carver's inspiration
summary: Asked how he came to jazz flute, Wess describes his teacher Henry L. Grant lending a flute and Wayman Carver of Chick Webb's band inspiring him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I would like to ask you if you could relate to us just how you were involved, you were one of the first to involve the flute in the big band context and in a jazz improvisation context. Tell us about that.
What led you to pick up that instrument as a jazz horn?

Oh well that started years ago when I was in high school. My teacher, Henry L. Grant, who was also Duke Ellington’s teacher and Billy Taylor, Dr. Billy Taylor and I studied with him. And he was the orchestra teacher you know. And he gave me a flute to take home you know. So I took it home and after fooling with it a while I realized that I couldn’t do it without a teacher, you know. And at the time, you know I couldn’t afford a teacher and there wasn’t one available that I knew of. So I said I’ll just let it rest until I can get to it you know. So at that time there was a fellow named Wayman Carver, who was in the Chick Webb orchestra. And he played with a group within the orchestra called the Little Chicks. And that inspired me to want to play the flute. Because he was the first that I know of to do it. So and he recorded a lot with Benny Carter and you know, the musicians that were recording at that time you know. So and then after I, well what happened actually I was studying the flute when I got a chance to study it under the GI bill I got a chance to go back to school and studied flute, so I did.
